Let D be the F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor whose cycle class is xi. In the standard terminology, D is an effective Cartier divisor whose associated line bundle is very ample. It is not the zero divisor: if D=0, then O_C(D)=O_C, whose global sections are the constants, so the complete linear system |D| is a single point and cannot give an embedding of the positive-dimensional curve C into projective space. Hence D is a nonzero effective 0-cycle. Write D = sum_{i=1}^r n_i y_i, where the y_i are the distinct closed points of C over F_{q^m} in the support of D and n_i are positive integers.

Now apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_166 with the base field F_{q^m} in place of F_q. It gives a Q_l-linear isomorphism tr_C: H^2_et(C_k,Q_l) -> Q_l(-1) (the Poincare duality trace, normalized by the degree of 0-cycles) such that for every closed point y of C over F_{q^m}, the trace of the cycle class of y on C_k is [kappa(y):F_{q^m}]. By Q_l-linearity, tr_C(xi) = sum_{i=1}^r n_i [kappa(y_i):F_{q^m}]. Each summand is a positive integer, so the sum is a positive integer. Since Q_l has characteristic 0, this integer is nonzero in Q_l, and therefore tr_C(xi) is a nonzero element of the one-dimensional Q_l-vector space Q_l(-1).

Since tr_C is an isomorphism, xi is nonzero. Equivalently, L(1)=xi and tr_C(L(1)) != 0, so L(1) != 0.

Finally, H^0_et(C_k,Q_l) is one-dimensional over Q_l, with basis 1, and H^2_et(C_k,Q_l) is one-dimensional over Q_l because tr_C identifies it with Q_l(-1). A linear map from a one-dimensional vector space to a one-dimensional vector space that sends a basis vector to a nonzero vector is an isomorphism. Thus L is an isomorphism.

This completes the proof for n=0 and n=1.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}, and let Y be a smooth geometrically connected very ample Cartier divisor on the base change X_k. Let i:Y -> X_k be the closed immersion. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Then the Gysin map i_!: H^1_et(Y_k,Q_ell) -> H^3_et(X_k,Q_ell) is surjective.
proof:
Let k = overline(F_q) and let U = X_k \ Y be the open complement of Y in X_k, with inclusion j: U -> X_k and closed immersion i: Y -> X_k. We prove that the Gysin map i_!: H^1_et(Y_k, Q_ell) -> H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell) (after identifying Tate twists with Q_ell) is surjective.

Step 1 (Descent of Y to a finite extension of F_{q^m}). We apply the descent lemma (eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_104_descent) with the prime power q^m in place of q; this is a legitimate specialization since q^m is a prime power. Concretely: (i) X is a scheme of finite type over F_{q^m}; (ii) the algebraic closure of F_{q^m} is k itself, because k = overline(F_q) is algebraically closed and contains F_{q^m}; (iii) Y is an integral closed subscheme of X x_{F_{q^m}} k = X_k, because Y is smooth over k (hence regular) and connected (Y is geometrically connected over the algebraically closed field k, hence connected), so Y is integral. Since X is smooth of pure dimension 2 over F_{q^m}, the descent lemma yields an integer r >= 1 and an integral closed subscheme Y_r of X_r := X x_{F_{q^m}} F_{q^{mr}} of codimension 1 (the same codimension as Y) such that Y_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k is isomorphic to Y as a closed subscheme of X_k.

Step 2 (The Gysin sequence over F_{q^{mr}}). We verify the hypotheses of the Gysin sequence lemma (eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement) with the prime power q^{mr} in place of q. (a) X_r = X x_{F_{q^m}} F_{q^{mr}} is smooth over F_{q^{mr}} (smoothness is preserved under base change), projective over F_{q^{mr}} (projectivity is preserved under base change), of pure dimension 2 (dimension is preserved under flat base change, and the field extension F_{q^{mr}}/F_{q^m} is flat), and geometrically connected over F_{q^{mr}}: by associativity of fiber products, X_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k = X x_{F_{q^m}} k = X_k, which is connected because X is geometrically connected over F_{q^m}. (b) Y_r is an integral closed subscheme of codimension 1 in X_r. Since X_r is regular (it is smooth over F_{q^{mr}}), Y_r is an effective Cartier divisor, hence an effective divisor defined over F_{q^{mr}}. It is smooth over F_{q^{mr}} because Y_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k = Y is smooth over k and smoothness descends under the faithfully flat morphism Spec k -> Spec F_{q^{mr}}. It has pure dimension 1 because it is integral of codimension 1 in X_r, which has pure dimension 2.

Thus the Gysin sequence lemma applies to the pair (X_r, Y_r) over F_{q^{mr}}, with U_r = X_r \ Y_r. It gives a long exact sequence of Q_ell-vector spaces
... -> H^{n-2}_et(Y_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k, Q_ell)(-1) ->^{i_!} H^n_et(X_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k, Q_ell) ->^{j^*} H^n_et(U_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k, Q_ell) -> ...,
where i_! is the Gysin homomorphism and j^* is restriction. By associativity of fiber products, X_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k = X_k, Y_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k = Y (as a closed subscheme of X_k), and U_r x_{F_{q^{mr}}} k = U. Hence the sequence identifies with
... -> H^{n-2}_et(Y, Q_ell)(-1) ->^{i_!} H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) ->^{j^*} H^n_et(U, Q_ell) -> ...,
where i_! is the Gysin homomorphism for i: Y -> X_k and j^* is restriction for j: U -> X_k. Taking n = 3, we obtain the exact segment
H^1_et(Y, Q_ell)(-1) ->^{i_!} H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell) ->^{j^*} H^3_et(U, Q_ell).
By exactness, im(i_!) = ker(j^*). In particular, if H^3_et(U, Q_ell) = 0, then j^* is the zero map, so ker(j^*) = H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell), and hence i_! is surjective.

Step 3 (Vanishing of H^3(U)). We show H^3_et(U, Q_ell) = 0 using the vanishing lemma (Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_337). First, X_k is an integral projective scheme of pure dimension 2 over k: X_k is smooth over k (smoothness is preserved under base change), hence regular; X_k is connected (X is geometrically connected over F_{q^m}); a connected regular scheme is integral (a regular scheme is a disjoint union of its irreducible components, since the intersection of two distinct components would be a non-regular point, so connectedness forces a single component); X_k is projective over k (projectivity is preserved under base change); and X_k has pure dimension 2 (dimension is preserved under flat base change). Now let L = O_{X_k}(Y), the line bundle associated to the Cartier divisor Y. Since Y is very ample on X_k, L is very ample, hence ample. Let s in H^0(X_k, L) = H^0(X_k, O_{X_k}(Y)) be the canonical section whose zero scheme is Y (the standard correspondence between effective Cartier divisors and sections of the associated line bundle). The vanishing locus V(s) = Y is a nonempty proper closed subscheme of X_k: Y is nonempty (it is a smooth curve of dimension 1) and proper (it has pure codimension 1 in the surface X_k, so Y != X_k). Applying the vanishing lemma with n = 1, we conclude that U = X_k \ V(s) = X_k \ Y is an affine k-scheme of Krull dimension 2, and H^m_et(U, Q_ell) = 0 for every integer m > 2. In particular, H^3_et(U, Q_ell) = 0.

Step 4 (Conclusion). From Step 2 we have the exact segment
H^1_et(Y, Q_ell)(-1) ->^{i_!} H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell) ->^{j^*} H^3_et(U, Q_ell),
and from Step 3, H^3_et(U, Q_ell) = 0. Hence j^* is the zero map, so ker(j^*) = H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell), and by exactness im(i_!) = ker(j^*) = H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell). Thus the map i_!: H^1_et(Y, Q_ell)(-1) -> H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell) is surjective.

Finally, we fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Under this identification, H^1_et(Y, Q_ell)(-1) is identified with H^1_et(Y, Q_ell), and the map i_!: H^1_et(Y, Q_ell)(-1) -> H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell) becomes the Gysin map i_!: H^1_et(Y_k, Q_ell) -> H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell) of the statement (the Gysin homomorphism is naturally i_!: H^1(Y) -> H^3(X_k)(1), which after the twist identification is i_!: H^1(Y) -> H^3(X_k)). Since the former map is surjective, the Gysin map i_!: H^1_et(Y_k, Q_ell) -> H^3_et(X_k, Q_ell) is surjective. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, X a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L cup product with xi, 0<=r<=d, P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}), and tr_X the Poincare duality trace. Then beta_r(x,y)=tr_X(x cup L^{d-r}y) on P^r satisfies beta_r(x,y)=(-1)^r beta_r(y,x) for all x,y in P^r.
proof:
Let x, y be arbitrary elements of P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k, Q_ell)). In particular x, y in H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell).

Recall the standard graded-commutativity of the cup product in etale cohomology with Q_ell-coefficients: for any a in H^p_et(X_k, Q_ell) and b in H^q_et(X_k, Q_ell), one has a cup b = (-1)^{pq} b cup a. This follows from the symmetric monoidal structure of the category of Q_ell-sheaves on X_k (the cup product is induced by the external product composed with the diagonal pullback, and the symmetry of the tensor product of sheaves introduces the sign (-1)^{pq}). The cup product is also associative: (a cup b) cup c = a cup (b cup c).

We now compute x cup L^{d-r} y step by step. Since L is cup product with xi in H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell), we have L^{d-r} y = xi^{d-r} cup y, where xi^{d-r} is the (d-r)-fold cup power of xi, an element of H^{2(d-r)}_et(X_k, Q_ell). (The degree of xi^{d-r} is 2(d-r), and L^{d-r} y lies in H^{r + 2(d-r)} = H^{2d-r}.)

Step 1. Swap x (degree r) with xi^{d-r} (degree 2(d-r)):
x cup xi^{d-r} cup y = (x cup xi^{d-r}) cup y = ((-1)^{r \cdot 2(d-r)} xi^{d-r} cup x) cup y.
Since r \cdot 2(d-r) is even (it is twice r(d-r)), the sign is +1, so
x cup xi^{d-r} cup y = (xi^{d-r} cup x) cup y = xi^{d-r} cup (x cup y)   [by associativity].

Step 2. Swap x (degree r) with y (degree r) inside the parentheses:
x cup y = (-1)^{r \cdot r} y cup x = (-1)^r y cup x.
Substituting:
xi^{d-r} cup (x cup y) = xi^{d-r} cup ((-1)^r y cup x) = (-1)^r xi^{d-r} cup (y cup x)   [by Q_ell-linearity of the cup product].

Step 3. Rewrite xi^{d-r} cup (y cup x) as (xi^{d-r} cup y) cup x by associativity, then swap xi^{d-r} (degree 2(d-r)) with y (degree r):
(xi^{d-r} cup y) cup x = ((-1)^{2(d-r) \cdot r} y cup xi^{d-r}) cup x.
Again 2(d-r) \cdot r is even, so the sign is +1, and
(xi^{d-r} cup y) cup x = (y cup xi^{d-r}) cup x = y cup xi^{d-r} cup x   [by associativity].

Combining Steps 1, 2, 3:
x cup xi^{d-r} cup y = (-1)^r y cup xi^{d-r} cup x.

Equivalently, since L^{d-r} y = xi^{d-r} cup y and L^{d-r} x = xi^{d-r} cup x (the same argument as in Step 1 shows xi^{d-r} cup x = x cup xi^{d-r} with no sign, because 2(d-r) is even), we have
x cup L^{d-r} y = (-1)^r y cup L^{d-r} x.

Now apply the Poincare duality trace tr_X: H^{2d}_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> Q_ell, which is a Q_ell-linear functional. Both sides of the identity above lie in H^{2d}_et(X_k, Q_ell) (the left side has degree r + (2d - r) = 2d, and the right side has degree r + (2d - r) = 2d). By Q_ell-linearity of tr_X:
tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y) = tr_X((-1)^r y cup L^{d-r} x) = (-1)^r tr_X(y cup L^{d-r} x).

By definition, beta_r(x,y) = tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y) and beta_r(y,x) = tr_X(y cup L^{d-r} x). Therefore
beta_r(x,y) = (-1)^r beta_r(y,x).

Since x, y were arbitrary elements of P^r, the identity holds for all x, y in P^r. This completes the proof.

Remark on the role of P^r: the computation above used only that x, y in H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell); the additional condition that x, y lie in ker(L^{d-r+1}) was not needed. Hence the symmetry identity a fortiori holds on P^r.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then there exists an integer n>=1 such that sum_{i>=0} (-1)^i Tr(F^n | H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell)) != 0.
proof: Put Q:=q^m. Then Q is a prime power, and k is also an algebraic closure of F_Q. We first note that all traces below are defined. The lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob is stated for a prime power q; applying it with the prime power Q in place of q to the constant sheaf Q_ell[0] on X_k with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism gives that each H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell and carries the canonical Q-power arithmetic Frobenius action. Since X is smooth projective and geometrically connected over F_Q, X_k is a smooth connected projective k-scheme, hence equidimensional; let d be its dimension. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_projective_cohomology_vanishes_above_twice_dimension, H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell)=0 for every i>2d, so every alternating sum appearing below is a finite sum. Next we produce a rational point over some finite extension of F_Q. Since X is nonempty, choose a nonempty affine open subscheme U=Spec A of X. Because X is of finite type over F_Q, A is a nonzero finitely generated F_Q-algebra. Choose a maximal ideal P of A (such an ideal exists since A is a nonzero unital ring) and put K=A/P. Then K is a field and is finitely generated as an F_Q-algebra by the images of a finite set of generators of A. We invoke the standard Zariski lemma: if E is a field and L is a field that is a finitely generated E-algebra, then L is a finite algebraic extension of E. Applying it with E=F_Q, K is finite over F_Q. Let r=[K:F_Q]; then r>=1. The closed point x:Spec K -> X has residue field K. Since K is a finite extension of F_Q of degree r, K has Q^r elements and is F_Q-isomorphic to F_{Q^r}; equivalently x is an F_{Q^r}-rational point of X. Hence #X(F_{Q^r})>=1. We now use the following standard Lefschetz fixed-point theorem. Let Y be a smooth projective variety over a finite field F_Q, let ell be a prime different from the characteristic of F_Q, let k be an algebraic closure of F_Q, and let G denote the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on H^i_et(Y_k,Q_ell). Then for every integer t>=1 one has #Y(F_{Q^t}) = sum_{i>=0} (-1)^i Tr(G^t | H^i_et(Y_k,Q_ell)), where the equality is in Q_ell and the sum is finite because the cohomology groups are finite-dimensional and vanish above 2 dim Y. Apply this theorem with Y=X, G=F, and t=r. The right-hand side is exactly sum_{i>=0} (-1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Therefore this alternating sum equals #X(F_{Q^r}) in Q_ell. Since #X(F_{Q^r}) is a positive integer, its image in Q_ell is nonzero. Taking n=r>=1 gives the desired nonzero alternating sum.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X be the inclusion. Then the restriction map i^*:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective.
proof:
We apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/f80cb4. That lemma states: let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, and let i:Y -> X be the inclusion. Then the restriction map i^*: H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective.

In the present statement we are given q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, X a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and Y a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, with inclusion i:Y -> X. Since d>=2, in particular d>=1. Thus all hypotheses of Miner/16d24b0281973336/f80cb4 are satisfied. The additional assumption that Y is geometrically connected is stronger than necessary for the cited lemma, but it is compatible with its hypotheses.

Therefore, by Miner/16d24b0281973336/f80cb4, the restriction map i^*: H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective. This is exactly the desired conclusion.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor on X, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every integer n with 0<=n<=d. For 0<=s<=d put P^s=ker(L^{d-s+1}:H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-s+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and put P^s=0 for s<0. Then the map from direct sum_{j>=0} L^j P^{d-2j} to H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) given by summing the images of L^j is an isomorphism.
proof: Let H^i denote H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell). We use the standard facts that H^i=0 for i<0 or i>2d, that all H^i are finite-dimensional over Q_ell, and that Poincare duality gives a perfect pairing H^a x H^{2d-a} -> Q_ell, (u,v) -> tr_X(u cup v). Since xi has degree 2, L commutes with every cohomology class. Put J=floor(d/2). For j=0,...,J set r_j=d-2j, P_j=P^{r_j}, and let V_j be the image of L^j:P_j -> H^d. For j>J the summand L^j P^{d-2j} is zero because P^{d-2j}=0, so the sum in the statement is the finite sum over 0<=j<=J. First, L^j:P_j -> V_j is an isomorphism. Surjectivity is by definition. If p in P_j satisfies L^j p=0, then L^{2j}p=0. By the hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n=r_j, the map L^{2j}:H^{r_j}->H^{2d-r_j}=H^{d+2j} is an isomorphism, hence injective, so p=0. Thus dim V_j=dim P_j. Next, the subspaces V_j are pairwise orthogonal for the pairing (x,y)->tr_X(x cup y) on H^d x H^d. Let j<j' and write x=L^j p in V_j, y=L^{j'} q in V_{j'}. Then tr_X(x cup y)=tr_X(p cup L^{j+j'} cup q)=tr_X((L^{j+j'} p) cup q). By definition p in P_j=ker(L^{2j+1}), and j+j' >= 2j+1, so L^{j+j'}p=0. Hence tr_X(x cup y)=0. By the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/4b7666, applied with r=d and the same j (0<=2j<=d), the form (x,y)->tr_X(x cup y) is nondegenerate on V_j x V_j. It follows that S=sum_{j=0}^J V_j is a direct sum. Indeed, if x_0+...+x_J=0 with x_j in V_j, fix i and pair this equality with an arbitrary y in V_i. Orthogonality gives tr_X(x_i cup y)=0 for all y in V_i; nondegeneracy on V_i then gives x_i=0. Therefore dim S=sum_j dim V_j=sum_j dim P_j. It remains to compute sum_j dim P_j. For each j, by the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/c671d8 applied with r=r_j, if Q_j=ker(L:H^{d+2j}->H^{d+2j+2}), then L^{2j}:P_j->Q_j is an isomorphism. Hence dim P_j=dim Q_j. We claim that L_j:=L:H^{d+2j}->H^{d+2j+2} is surjective for every j. If d-2j-2<0, then d+2j+2>2d, so H^{d+2j+2}=0 and L_j is surjective. If a=d-2j-2>=0, the hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n=a says L^{2j+2}:H^a->H^{2d-a}=H^{d+2j+2} is an isomorphism. Therefore f:=L:H^a->H^{a+2}=H^{d-2j} is injective: if f u=0 then L^{2j+2}u=0, so u=0. Now use Poincare duality. Let A=H^a, B=H^{a+2}=H^{d-2j}, C=H^{d+2j}, D=H^{d+2j+2}. The pairings A x D and B x C given by tr_X are perfect. The adjoint f^*:C->D of f is defined by tr_X((f u) cup z)=tr_X(u cup f^* z) for u in A and z in C. Since f u = u cup xi and L has degree 2, tr_X((f u) cup z)=tr_X(u cup (L z)), so f^* z = L z. Thus f^* is exactly L_j. We prove the needed linear algebra fact that f^* is surjective. Let E=im f subset B. Because B x C is perfect, the map C -> E^* sending z to (e -> tr_X(e cup z)) is surjective; its kernel is E^perp={z in C: tr_X(w cup z)=0 for all w in E}, so dim E^perp = dim C - dim E. But ker f^* = E^perp, since z is in ker f^* exactly when tr_X((f u) cup z)=0 for all u in A. Since f is injective, dim E=dim A. Perfectness of A x D gives dim D=dim A. Therefore dim im f^* = dim C - dim ker f^* = dim C - (dim C - dim A)=dim A=dim D, so f^* is surjective. This proves the claim. With L_j surjective, we have an exact sequence 0 -> Q_j -> H^{d+2j} -> H^{d+2j+2} -> 0, so dim Q_j = dim H^{d+2j} - dim H^{d+2j+2}. Hence sum_{j=0}^J dim P_j = sum_{j=0}^J dim Q_j = sum_{j=0}^J (dim H^{d+2j} - dim H^{d+2j+2}) = dim H^d - dim H^{d+2J+2}. If d=2J is even, then d+2J+2=2d+2; if d=2J+1 is odd, then d+2J+2=2d+1. In both cases the degree is greater than 2d, so H^{d+2J+2}=0. Thus sum_j dim P_j = dim H^d. Consequently dim S = dim H^d. Since S is a subspace of H^d, S=H^d. The canonical map from the direct sum of the subspaces L^j P^{d-2j} to H^d is therefore an isomorphism. This is exactly the map in the statement.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Suppose that for every integer n with 0<=n<=d, the operator F on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Then for every integer i>=0, the operator F on H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Set q' = q^m. Since q' is a prime power and overline(F_{q'}) = overline(F_q) = k, we may apply the cited lemmas with q' in place of q whenever their statement uses q=p^a. Write F_i for the restriction of F to H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell). First, by the vanishing lemma for projective cohomology, H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell)=0 for every i>2d, because X_k is projective over k and equidimensional of dimension d. The operator on the zero vector space is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), since the zero vector space has an empty basis and the corresponding matrix is the empty diagonal matrix. Thus it suffices to treat 0<=i<=2d. For 0<=i<=d the conclusion is exactly the hypothesis. Now assume d+1<=i<=2d and put j=2d-i, so 0<=j<=d-1. By the finiteness lemma for Frobenius cohomology, applied to the constant sheaf Q_ell with its natural Frobenius structure, H^j and H^i are finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces. By the Frobenius invertibility lemma, F_j and F_i are invertible Q_ell-linear operators. Let c = q^{md}. By the Frobenius-equivariant Poincare duality lemma, the pairing <x,y> = tr(x cup y) from H^j x H^i to Q_ell(-d) is a perfect Q_ell-bilinear pairing and satisfies <F_j x, F_i y> = c <x,y> for all x in H^j and y in H^i. Fix a nonzero element xi of the one-dimensional Q_ell-vector space Q_ell(-d). Perfectness gives a Q_ell-linear isomorphism Psi: H^i -> Hom_Q_ell(H^j,Q_ell) characterized by <x,y> = Psi(y)(x) xi for all x,y. For y in H^i and x in H^j we compute Psi(F_i y)(F_j x) xi = <F_j x, F_i y> = c <x,y> = c Psi(y)(x) xi. Since xi is nonzero, this is equivalent to Psi(F_i y)(F_j x) = c Psi(y)(x). Because F_j is invertible, every w in H^j can be written uniquely as w = F_j x with x = F_j^{-1} w. Substituting x = F_j^{-1} w gives Psi(F_i y)(w) = c Psi(y)(F_j^{-1} w) for all w in H^j. In other words, Psi(F_i y) = c (F_j^{-1})^vee Psi(y), where (F_j^{-1})^vee is the transpose on the dual space, defined by (F_j^{-1})^vee(phi)(w) = phi(F_j^{-1} w). Hence Psi F_i = c (F_j^{-1})^vee Psi, and because Psi is an isomorphism, F_i is Q_ell-similar to c (F_j^{-1})^vee. It remains to show that c (F_j^{-1})^vee is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). By hypothesis, F_j is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). By the equivalence lemma, F_j is semisimple. By the inverse lemma, F_j^{-1} is semisimple. By the transpose lemma, (F_j^{-1})^vee is semisimple. By the scalar-multiple lemma, c (F_j^{-1})^vee is semisimple. By the equivalence lemma again, semisimple means diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Finally, similarity preserves diagonalizability: if A = P D P^{-1} over overline(Q_ell) with D diagonal, then S^{-1} A S = (S^{-1} P) D (S^{-1} P)^{-1} is also diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Applying this with A = c (F_j^{-1})^vee and S = Psi^{-1} shows that F_i is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). This completes the range d+1<=i<=2d, and together with the previous ranges proves the statement for every i>=0.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X be the inclusion. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1), identify Tate twists with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), and let L be cup product with xi. Let W be the image of i^*:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell), and let tr_Y:H^{2d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell be the Poincare duality trace. Then the Q_ell-bilinear form (a,b)->tr_Y(a cup b) on W is nondegenerate if and only if L:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is injective.
proof: Let r = i^* : H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_{et}(Y_k,Q_ell) and let W = im(r). By Miner/16d24b0281973336/79a472, r is injective. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor to X over F_{q^m}, with the same choice of nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and the same identification of Tate twists, i.e. with the prime power q^m in place of q. It gives a Gysin map i_! : H^{d-1}_{et}(Y_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d+1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell) characterized by tr_X(i_! a cup b) = tr_Y(a cup i^* b) for a in H^{d-1}_{et}(Y_k,Q_ell) and b in H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell), and the projection formula i_!(i^* x) = x cup xi for x in H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell). For x,y in H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell), the characterizing property with a = r y and b = x gives tr_X(i_! r y cup x) = tr_Y(r y cup r x). Graded commutativity gives tr_X(x cup i_! r y) = (-1)^{(d-1)(d+1)} tr_X(i_! r y cup x) = (-1)^{(d-1)(d+1)} tr_Y(r y cup r x) = (-1)^{(d-1)(d+1)+(d-1)^2} tr_Y(r x cup r y) = (-1)^{2d(d-1)} tr_Y(r x cup r y) = tr_Y(r x cup r y). By the projection formula, i_! r y = L y, so we obtain the identity tr_Y(r x cup r y) = tr_X(x cup L y). Define B_Y(a,b)=tr_Y(a cup b) on W and B_X(u,v)=tr_X(u cup L v) on H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell). Then B_Y(r x, r y) = B_X(x,y). Now suppose B_Y is nondegenerate. If x is in ker(L), then for every y, B_Y(r x, r y) = B_X(x,y) = tr_X(x cup L y). Since L y = y cup xi and L x = x cup xi, and xi has degree 2, we have x cup L y = x cup y cup xi = x cup xi cup y = L x cup y. Hence B_Y(r x, r y) = tr_X(L x cup y) = 0. Since W is exactly the set of elements r y, this says B_Y(r x, W)=0. Nondegeneracy gives r x=0, and injectivity of r gives x=0. Thus L is injective. Conversely, suppose L is injective. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, the Poincare duality pairing H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell) x H^{d+1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell, after the fixed identification of Tate twists with Q_ell, is perfect; in particular the two vector spaces have the same finite dimension. Therefore the injective map L is an isomorphism. Let w in W have B_Y(w,W)=0. Write w=r a. For every b, 0=B_Y(r a,r b)=B_X(a,b)=tr_X(a cup L b). Since L is onto, the classes L b run through all H^{d+1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell), so tr_X(a cup c)=0 for every c in H^{d+1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell). By the perfect Poincare pairing, a=0, so w=0. If instead B_Y(W,w)=0, then for every b, 0=B_Y(r b,r a)=B_X(b,a)=tr_X(b cup L a). By the perfect Poincare pairing, L a=0; since L is injective, a=0, hence w=0. Thus both radicals of B_Y on W are zero, i.e. B_Y is nondegenerate. This proves the equivalence.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), and let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_{q^m}. Then every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}.
proof: Let Q=q^m. Since q=p^a, Q is a prime power and k=overline(F_q)=overline(F_Q). We invoke the classical theorem of Weil for curves over finite fields, equivalently the i=1 case of the Weil-Deligne purity theorem stated for arithmetic Frobenius: if Q is a prime power, C is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_Q, ell is a prime different from the residue characteristic of Q, and k is an algebraic closure of F_Q, then the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell) is semisimple, and every eigenvalue of its action on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) has Weil absolute value Q^{1/2}; that is, for every embedding iota: overline(Q_ell) -> C and every such eigenvalue alpha, |iota(alpha)|=Q^{1/2}. This standard theorem is invoked as such; it is not derived from, and not attributed to, the separate fact that the constant sheaf is pure of weight 0. Apply it with C as in the statement and i=1. The hypotheses are satisfied: C is smooth projective and geometrically connected over F_{q^m}=F_Q, ell != p, and k is an algebraic closure. Hence every eigenvalue alpha of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value Q^{1/2}. Finally Q^{1/2}=(q^m)^{1/2}=q^{m/2}, which is the required absolute value.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor on X, and let L be cup product with xi. Then L^d:H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism.
proof: Set Q = q^m. Since q = p^a, we have Q = p^{am}, so Q is a prime power. Moreover, overline(F_Q) = overline(F_{q^m}) = overline(F_q) = k. The variety X is smooth, projective, geometrically connected, and of pure dimension d >= 2 over F_{q^m} = F_Q. The given divisor is an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor on X, hence a very ample divisor on X defined over F_Q. Apply the proved lemma Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_358_top_degree to this situation, using the same fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) to identify the cycle class xi in H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell). That lemma states that the cup-product map H^0_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d}_et(X_k, Q_ell), x |-> x cup xi^d, is an isomorphism. By definition, L is cup product with xi, so L^d is exactly the map x |-> x cup xi^d. Therefore L^d: H^0_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell), and let G be the inverse of F. Suppose that for every integer i>=0, the operator F on H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Then for every integer i>=0, the operator G on H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Let Q=q^m. Since q is a prime power, Q is a prime power, and k=overline(F_q)=overline(F_Q). The variety X is smooth projective over F_Q, hence proper over F_Q. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob with Q in place of q, with K the constant sheaf Q_ell on X_k equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism. It follows that for every integer i>=0, V_i:=H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space and the induced Q_ell-linear arithmetic Frobenius F_i:V_i->V_i is an automorphism. This F_i is precisely the restriction of the given operator F to V_i. Since G is defined to be the inverse of F, its restriction to V_i is G_i=F_i^{-1}. Fix i>=0. If V_i=0, the desired diagonalizability of G_i over overline(Q_ell) is vacuous, so assume V_i is nonzero. By hypothesis, F_i is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), meaning the base-changed operator on V_i tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) is diagonalizable. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_5, for a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space, a linear operator is semisimple if and only if its base change to overline(Q_ell) is diagonalizable; hence F_i is semisimple on V_i. Since V_i is finite-dimensional and F_i is invertible, eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_4 implies that F_i is semisimple if and only if F_i^{-1} is semisimple. Therefore G_i=F_i^{-1} is semisimple on V_i. Applying eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_5 again to G_i, semisimplicity of G_i on V_i is equivalent to diagonalizability of G_i over overline(Q_ell). Thus G_i is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Since i was arbitrary, the conclusion holds for every integer i>=0.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), and let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_{q^m}. Then every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}.
proof:
Proof. We establish the statement by identifying it, clause by clause, with the statement of a proved lemma in the library, and then applying that proved lemma. No new mathematics is needed because the exact result has already been proved.

Step 1 (the matching proved lemma). The proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/3cb9b7 states: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), and let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_{q^m}. Then every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}.

Step 2 (comparison of the statements). The statement to be proved in the present lemma is: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), and let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_{q^m}. Then every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}. We compare the two statements clause by clause. Hypotheses: in both statements q=p^a is a prime power, ell is a prime with ell != p, m is an integer with m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and C is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_{q^m}; the hypotheses are identical. Conclusions: in both statements the conclusion is that every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}; the conclusions are identical. Hence the two statements are word-for-word the same proposition.

Step 3 (no circularity). The dependency record of the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/3cb9b7 is empty: its proof cites no lemmas and no references at all. Its proof is therefore self-contained and in particular cannot depend on the present lemma. Citing it here is hence not circular; the present lemma is closed by an already-established, independent proof of the identical proposition.

Step 4 (application). Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and C be as in the present lemma. These data satisfy the hypotheses of Miner/16d24b0281973336/3cb9b7 verbatim. Applying that proved lemma to this data yields exactly the desired conclusion: every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}.

This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, let r be an integer with 0<=r<=d, and put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). Suppose F(P^r)=P^r and every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Then every eigenvalue of F|_{P^r}, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.
proof:
Let V = H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ). We first record that V is a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-vector space. Indeed, X is a smooth projective variety of pure dimension d over the finite field F_{q^m}; by Grothendieck's finiteness theorem for ℓ-adic cohomology, each group H^i_et(X_k, Z/ℓ^n) is a finite abelian group for every i ≥ 0 and n ≥ 1, so H^i_et(X_k, Z_ℓ) = lim_n H^i_et(X_k, Z/ℓ^n) is a finitely generated Z_ℓ-module, and H^i_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) = H^i_et(X_k, Z_ℓ) ⊗_{Z_ℓ} Q_ℓ is a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-vector space. In particular dim_{Q_ℓ} V < ∞. By the standard theory of Frobenius on ℓ-adic cohomology (the pullback map (id_X × σ)^* for the q^m-power automorphism σ of k), F is a Q_ℓ-linear automorphism of V.

Next we verify that P^r is a Q_ℓ-subspace of V. The class ξ lies in H^2_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), and cup product with ξ gives a Q_ℓ-linear map L: H^i_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{i+2}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) for each i (this is because cup product is Q_ℓ-bilinear and ξ is a fixed Q_ℓ-class). The iterated map L^{d-r+1}: V = H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{r+2(d-r+1)}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) = H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) is therefore a Q_ℓ-linear map (a composition of Q_ℓ-linear maps). Its kernel P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}) is hence a Q_ℓ-subspace of V.

By hypothesis, F(P^r) = P^r, so P^r is an F-stable subspace of V.

We now prove that every eigenvalue of F|_{P^r} viewed in overline(Q_ℓ) is an eigenvalue of F viewed in overline(Q_ℓ). Let s = dim_{Q_ℓ} P^r and n = dim_{Q_ℓ} V, with 0 ≤ s ≤ n. Choose a Q_ℓ-basis e_1, …, e_s of P^r and extend it to a Q_ℓ-basis e_1, …, e_s, e_{s+1}, …, e_n of V. With respect to this basis, the matrix of F takes the block upper-triangular form
  F = [ A  B ]
      [ 0  C ],
where A is the s × s matrix representing the restriction F|_{P^r} with respect to the basis e_1, …, e_s of P^r, and C is an (n−s) × (n−s) matrix. The lower-left block is the zero matrix because F(P^r) ⊆ P^r: for each j ≤ s, F(e_j) ∈ P^r, so F(e_j) is a Q_ℓ-linear combination of e_1, …, e_s, contributing no component in the e_{s+1}, …, e_n directions.

The characteristic polynomial of F is χ_F(t) = det(tI_n − F). For a block upper-triangular matrix, the determinant is the product of the determinants of the diagonal blocks, so
  χ_F(t) = det(tI_s − A) · det(tI_{n−s} − C).
(To verify this formula explicitly: the matrix tI_n − F has the same block form [tI_s − A, B; 0, tI_{n−s} − C]. One may compute its determinant by expanding along the zero block, or by observing that [tI_s − A, B; 0, tI_{n−s} − C] = [I_s, B(tI_{n−s}−C)^{-1}; 0, I_{n−s}] · [tI_s − A, 0; 0, tI_{n−s} − C] when tI_{n−s}−C is invertible, and then extending by polynomial identity; in all cases det(tI_n − F) = det(tI_s − A)·det(tI_{n−s} − C).)

In particular, det(tI_s − A) divides χ_F(t) in Q_ℓ[t].

Now extend scalars from Q_ℓ to overline(Q_ℓ). The eigenvalues of F|_{P^r} in overline(Q_ℓ) are precisely the roots in overline(Q_ℓ) of the polynomial det(tI_s − A) ∈ Q_ℓ[t] ⊂ overline(Q_ℓ)[t], and the eigenvalues of F in overline(Q_ℓ) are precisely the roots in overline(Q_ℓ) of χ_F(t) ∈ Q_ℓ[t] ⊂ overline(Q_ℓ)[t]. Since det(tI_s − A) divides χ_F(t) in Q_ℓ[t], and hence in overline(Q_ℓ)[t], every root of det(tI_s − A) in overline(Q_ℓ) is a root of χ_F(t) in overline(Q_ℓ). Therefore every eigenvalue of F|_{P^r} viewed in overline(Q_ℓ) is an eigenvalue of F viewed in overline(Q_ℓ).

By hypothesis, every eigenvalue of F on V = H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), viewed in overline(Q_ℓ), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Since every eigenvalue of F|_{P^r} in overline(Q_ℓ) is among the eigenvalues of F in overline(Q_ℓ), it follows that every eigenvalue of F|_{P^r}, viewed in overline(Q_ℓ), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.

This completes the proof. (In the degenerate case P^r = {0}, the operator F|_{P^r} is the zero map on the zero-dimensional space and has no eigenvalues, so the conclusion holds vacuously; in the case P^r = V, the restriction is F itself and the conclusion is the hypothesis.)

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let V=H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell), let F be the induced q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on V, let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on V, put G(x,y)=beta(x,Fy)+(-1)^d q^{md} beta(x,F^{-1}y), and let U be the unipotent part of F. Then G(Ux,Uy)=G(x,y) for all x,y in V.
proof:
I have confirmed all the lemmas I need. The proof strategy is:

1. **Key fact (lemma `f31bc8`):** On $W=H^d_{	ext{ét}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)$, the unipotent part $F_u$ of the Frobenius satisfies $ eta(F_u x,F_u y)= eta(x,y)$ — i.e. it is a $ eta$-isometry.
2. **Base change to $V=W\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$:** the unipotent part commutes with base change (using the polynomial characterization `df0feb` + uniqueness of the Jordan–Chevalley decomposition), so $U=U_W\otimes 1$ is also a $ eta_V$-isometry.
3. **Computation:** since $F$ and $U$ commute, $G(Ux,Uy)=G(x,y)$.

Let me write the complete proof.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/fda972",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Miner/16d24b0281973336/f31bc8", "Miner/16d24b0281973336/df0feb"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "Let W = H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell). Let F_W be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on W, and write its Jordan-Chevalley decomposition as F_W = S_W U_W = U_W S_W with S_W semisimple and U_W unipotent. Let beta_W be the Poincare duality pairing on W. The space in the statement is V = W tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell); the Frobenius F on V is F_W tensor 1, and beta denotes the Poincare duality pairing on V, which is the Q_ell-bilinear extension of beta_W (both pairings are defined by cup product followed by the Poincare trace, and both operations commute with base change). Let U be the unipotent part of F on V.

Step 1 (U_W is a beta_W-isometry). By the lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/f31bc8 (whose hypotheses match ours exactly: q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, X smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, Tate twists identified with Q_ell), we have
    beta_W(U_W a, U_W b) = beta_W(a, b)   for all a, b in W.
So U_W is a beta_W-isometry.

Step 2 (base change: U = U_W tensor 1). By the lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/df0feb applied to F_W on the finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space W (characteristic 0), there exists a polynomial P in Q_ell[t] with U_W = P(F_W). On V we have F = F_W tensor 1, so
    P(F) = P(F_W tensor 1) = P(F_W) tensor 1 = U_W tensor 1.
The operator P(F) = U_W tensor 1 is unipotent on V: U_W is unipotent, so U_W - I_W is nilpotent, and (U_W tensor 1) - I_V = (U_W - I_W) tensor 1 is nilpotent. Also F_W = S_W U_W with S_W semisimple, hence
    F = F_W tensor 1 = (S_W tensor 1)(U_W tensor 1) = (S_W tensor 1) P(F),
where S_W tensor 1 is semisimple on V: semisimplicity is preserved under field extension in characteristic 0, because an operator over a field K of characteristic 0 is semisimple if and only if it is diagonalizable over the algebraic closure of K, and a basis of eigenvectors over the algebraic closure of K is a fortiori a basis of eigenvectors over the algebraic closure of any extension. Finally, S_W tensor 1 commutes with P(F): since S_W commutes with F_W (Jordan-Chevalley decomposition), S_W commutes with P(F_W)) for every polynomial P, and therefore S_W tensor 1 commutes with P(F) = P(F_W) tensor 1. Thus F = (S_W tensor 1) P(F) is a Jordan-Chevalley decomposition of F on V (semisimple part S_W tensor 1, unipotent part P(F)). By uniqueness of the Jordan-Chevalley decomposition over the field overline(Q_ell) of characteristic 0 (the unipotent part of an invertible operator is a polynomial in the operator, hence is uniquely determined by the operator), the unipotent part of F is
    U = P(F) = U_W tensor 1.

Step 3 (U is a beta_V-isometry). Take x, y in V and write x = sum_i a_i tensor r_i and y = sum_j b_j tensor s_j with a_i, b_j in W and r_i, s_j in overline(Q_ell). Using U = U_W tensor 1 and that beta_V is the bilinear extension of beta_W,
    beta_V(Ux, Uy) = beta_V((U_W tensor 1)(sum_i a_i tensor r_i), (U_W tensor 1)(sum_j b_j tensor s_j))
    = beta_V(sum_i U_W a_i tensor r_i, sum_j U_W b_j tensor s_j)
    = sum_{i,j} beta_W(U_W a_i, U_W b_j) r_i s_j
    = sum_{i,j} beta_W(a_i, b_j) r_i s_j        (by Step 1)
    = beta_V(x, y).
Hence beta_V(Ux, Uy) = beta_V(x, y) for all x, y in V; in particular, for every z in V, beta_V(Ux, Uz) = beta_V(x, z).

Step 4 (F and U commute). Since F_W and U_W commute on W (Jordan-Chevalley decomposition),
    F U = (F_W tensor 1)(U_W tensor 1) = (F_W U_W) tensor 1 = (U_W F_W) tensor 1 = (U_W tensor 1)(F_W tensor 1) = U F.
F is invertible (it is the Frobenius automorphism), and since U_W commutes with F_W, U_W also commutes with F_W^{-1} (if AB = BA with B invertible, then A B^{-1} = B^{-1} A); hence U commutes with F^{-1} on V. Therefore, for every y in V,
    F(Uy) = U(Fy)   and   F^{-1}(Uy) = U(F^{-1} y).

Step 5 (conclusion). For x, y in V, using the definition of G, the commutativity from Step 4, and the isometry from Step 3,
    G(Ux, Uy) = beta_V(Ux, F(Uy)) + (-1)^d q^{md} beta_V(Ux, F^{-1}(Uy))
    = beta_V(Ux, U(Fy)) + (-1)^d q^{md} beta_V(Ux, U(F^{-1} y))
    = beta_V(x, Fy) + (-1)^d q^{md} beta_V(x, F^{-1} y)
    = G(x, y).
This proves G(Ux, Uy) = G(x, y) for all x, y in V, as required."
}

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor on X, let L be cup product with xi, and for 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then F(P^r)=P^r for every integer r with 0<=r<=d.
proof:
Proof. Set q_0 := q^m. Since F_{q^m} is a finite extension of F_q contained in overline(F_q), and overline(F_q) is algebraically closed, the field overline(F_q) is an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}. Hence k = overline(F_q) = overline(F_{q^m}) = overline(F_{q_0}). We now apply the proved lemmas with the prime power q_0 = q^m in place of q.

Step 1 (Frobenius-Lefschetz commutation and stability). The variety X is a smooth projective variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m} = F_{q_0} (the hypothesis that X is geometrically connected is an additional assumption and is not needed for what follows). The divisor whose cycle class is xi is very ample and defined over F_{q^m} = F_{q_0}. By definition, F is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, i.e. F = (id_X x sigma)^* where sigma: k -> k is given by sigma(u) = u^{q^m}; this is precisely the q_0-power arithmetic Frobenius appearing in the statement of eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable. The class xi is the cycle class of this divisor, viewed as an element of H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell) via the fixed identification Q_ell(1) = Q_ell, and L is cup product with xi. For 0 <= m <= d, the subspace P^m = ker(L^{d-m+1}: H^m_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d-m+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)) in the statement of that lemma is, under the renaming m -> r, definitionally identical to the P^r of the target statement: the exponent d-m+1 equals d-r+1 and the codomain H^{2d-m+2} equals H^{2d-r+2}.

Applying eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable with q_0, we obtain F o L = q_0 L o F on every H^m_et(X_k, Q_ell), and consequently, for every 0 <= m <= d, the subspace P^m is stable under both F and F^{-1}. Concretely this gives, for every 0 <= m <= d: (i) F(P^m) is contained in P^m; and (ii) F^{-1}(P^m) is contained in P^m.

Step 2 (invertibility of F). By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, applied with the prime power q_0 (X is a scheme over F_{q_0}, k = overline(F_{q_0}), sigma(u) = u^{q_0}), the pullback F = (id_X x sigma)^* is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) for every i >= 0, and its inverse is the geometric Frobenius (id_X x sigma^{-1})^*. In particular, for each 0 <= r <= d, the map F: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) is an invertible Q_ell-linear map, so for every x in H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) the element F^{-1}(x) is well defined and satisfies F(F^{-1}(x)) = x.

Step 3 (conclusion). Fix an integer r with 0 <= r <= d.

Inclusion F(P^r) is contained in P^r: this is exactly the statement (i) with m = r, obtained in Step 1.

Inclusion P^r is contained in F(P^r): let x be an element of P^r. By Step 2, z := F^{-1}(x) is a well-defined element of H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell). By the stability (ii) with m = r, since x is in P^r we have z = F^{-1}(x) in P^r. Then x = F(F^{-1}(x)) = F(z) with z in P^r, so x lies in F(P^r). Hence P^r is contained in F(P^r).

Combining the two inclusions gives F(P^r) = P^r.

Since r was an arbitrary integer with 0 <= r <= d, the equality F(P^r) = P^r holds for every such r. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let S be a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}, let D be a smooth geometrically connected very ample divisor on S defined over F_{q^m}, and let i:D->S be the inclusion. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let i_!:H^0_et(D_k,Q_ell)->H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell) be the Gysin map, and let F_0 and F_2 be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^0_et(D_k,Q_ell) and H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell), respectively. Then F_2 ∘ i_! = q^m i_! ∘ F_0.
proof: Set Q=q^m. Since D is a smooth divisor on the surface S, D is a closed integral subscheme of S of pure codimension 1, hence a codimension-one cycle on S over F_Q. Let ξ be the chosen nonzero element of Q_ℓ(1). Let cl(D)∈H^2_et(S_k,Q_ℓ(1)) be the ℓ-adic cycle class of D, and let c_D∈H^2_et(S_k,Q_ℓ) be the unique element with cl(D)=c_D⊗ξ under the identification H^2_et(S_k,Q_ℓ(1))=H^2_et(S_k,Q_ℓ)⊗_{Q_ℓ}Q_ℓ(1). By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_78, with its prime power q specialized to Q, with j=1 and z=D, the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius F_Q on H^2_et(S_k,Q_ℓ(1)) fixes cl(D), and F_Q acts on Q_ℓ(1) by multiplication by Q^{-1}. Thus F_Q(c_D⊗ξ)=F_Q(c_D)⊗Q^{-1}ξ=c_D⊗ξ, so F_Q(c_D)=Q c_D. The Q-power arithmetic Frobenius on the untwisted cohomology H^2_et(S_k,Q_ℓ) is exactly F_2, hence F_2(c_D)=q^m c_D. For a smooth closed immersion of relative codimension one, the Gysin map i_!:H^0_et(D_k,Q_ℓ)→H^2_et(S_k,Q_ℓ(1)) sends the fundamental class 1 to the cycle class of D; after the fixed identification Q_ℓ(1)≅Q_ℓ this is the Gysin map in the statement, so i_!1=c_D. Next, F_0 is the identity: D is geometrically connected, so D_k is connected, hence H^0_et(D_k,Q_ℓ) is the space of locally constant Q_ℓ-valued functions on D_k, canonically Q_ℓ, and the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acts by pullback on these functions, fixing every constant function. Finally, let a∈H^0_et(D_k,Q_ℓ) and write a=λ·1 with λ∈Q_ℓ. Then F_2(i_!a)=F_2(λ c_D)=λ F_2(c_D)=λ q^m c_D, while q^m i_!(F_0 a)=q^m i_!(λ·1)=λ q^m c_D. Therefore F_2∘i_!=q^m i_!∘F_0 as Q_ℓ-linear maps.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->mathbb C be an embedding, let V and W be finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces, let T_V and T_W be Q_ell-linear automorphisms, and let phi:V->W be a Q_ell-linear injection such that T_W phi=phi T_V. Suppose there exists a positive definite Hermitian form h_W on W tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} mathbb C such that h_W((T_W tensor id)x,(T_W tensor id)y)=q^m h_W(x,y) for all x,y in W tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} mathbb C. Then the form h_V(x,y)=h_W(phi x,phi y) is a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} mathbb C satisfying h_V((T_V tensor id)x,(T_V tensor id)y)=q^m h_V(x,y) for all x,y in V tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} mathbb C.
proof:
Proof. Let C = \mathbb C and regard C as a \mathbb Q_\ell-vector space via the embedding \sigma|_{\mathbb Q_\ell}: \mathbb Q_\ell \hookrightarrow \mathbb C (the restriction of \sigma to \mathbb Q_\ell, which is an embedding since \mathbb Q_\ell \subset \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell). Write V_C = V \otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell, \sigma} C and W_C = W \otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell, \sigma} C. These are finite-dimensional C-vector spaces of dimensions \dim_{\mathbb Q_\ell}(V) and \dim_{\mathbb Q_\ell}(W) respectively. Every element of V_C (resp. W_C) is a finite sum of simple tensors v \otimes c (resp. w \otimes c) with v \in V (resp. w \in W) and c \in C, and the C-vector space structure is given by (v \otimes c)\cdot c' = v \otimes (c c') for c' \in C. In particular the simple tensors span V_C (resp. W_C) as a C-vector space.

Step 1 (base change of \phi). Consider the map B: V \times C \to W_C defined by B(v, c) = \phi(v) \otimes c (the codomain is the \mathbb Q_\ell-vector space W_C = W \otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell} C, not the product W \times C). We verify B is \mathbb Q_\ell-bilinear. For v, v' \in V and c, c' \in C:
- Additivity in the first variable: B(v+v', c) = \phi(v+v') \otimes c = (\phi(v)+\phi(v')) \otimes c = (\phi(v)\otimes c) + (\phi(v')\otimes c) = B(v,c) + B(v',c).
- Additivity in the second variable: B(v, c+c') = \phi(v) \otimes (c+c') = (\phi(v)\otimes c) + (\phi(v)\otimes c') = B(v,c) + B(v,c').
- \mathbb Q_\ell-linearity: for a \in \mathbb Q_\ell, B(av, c) = \phi(av) \otimes c = (a\phi(v)) \otimes c = \phi(v) \otimes (a c) = B(v, a c), where the third equality uses the balancing relation (a w)\otimes c = w\otimes (a c) in W \otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell} C (with a c = \sigma(a)\,c the \mathbb Q_\ell-scalar multiple of c in C). Since a B(v,c) = a(\phi(v)\otimes c) = \phi(v)\otimes (a c) as well, we have B(av,c) = a\,B(v,c) = B(v, a c), so B is \mathbb Q_\ell-bilinear.

By the universal property of the tensor product, B induces a unique \mathbb Q_\ell-linear map \phi_K: V_C \to W_C such that \phi_K(v \otimes c) = \phi(v) \otimes c for all v \in V, c \in C. We now show \phi_K is C-linear. For a simple tensor v \otimes c and any c' \in C:
\phi_K((v \otimes c)\cdot c') = \phi_K(v \otimes (c c')) = \phi(v) \otimes (c c') = (\phi(v)\otimes c)\cdot c' = \phi_K(v \otimes c)\cdot c'.
Since the simple tensors span V_C as a C-vector space, this identity extends to all x \in V_C: \phi_K(x\cdot c') = \phi_K(x)\cdot c' for every c' \in C. Hence \phi_K is C-linear. (Equivalently, \phi_K = \phi \otimes \mathrm{id}_C is the canonical C-linear base change of the \mathbb Q_\ell-linear map \phi to C.)

Step 2 (injectivity of \phi_K). Let {e_1, \dots, e_n} be a \mathbb Q_\ell-basis of V, where n = \dim_{\mathbb Q_\ell}(V). Because \phi is injective, the vectors \phi(e_1), \dots, \phi(e_n) are linearly independent in W; extend them to a \mathbb Q_\ell-basis {\phi(e_1), \dots, \phi(e_n), f_{n+1}, \dots, f_N} of W, where N = \dim_{\mathbb Q_\ell}(W) \ge n. Since V \cong \mathbb Q_\ell^n via the basis {e_i}, base change gives V_C \cong C^n via e_i \otimes 1 \mapsto (the i-th standard basis vector), so {e_1 \otimes 1, \dots, e_n \otimes 1} is a C-basis of V_C; similarly {\phi(e_1)\otimes 1, \dots, \phi(e_n)\otimes 1, f_{n+1}\otimes 1, \dots, f_N\otimes 1} is a C-basis of W_C. The map \phi_K sends each basis vector e_i \otimes 1 of V_C to \phi(e_i)\otimes 1, and the set {\phi(e_1)\otimes 1, \dots, \phi(e_n)\otimes 1} is linearly independent in W_C (it is a subset of the C-basis of W_C). A C-linear map that sends a basis to a linearly independent set is injective, so \phi_K is injective.

Step 3 (intertwining after base change). The hypothesis gives T_W \circ \phi = \phi \circ T_V as \mathbb Q_\ell-linear maps V \to W. For a simple tensor v \otimes c \in V_C:
(T_W \otimes \mathrm{id}_C)(\phi_K(v \otimes c)) = (T_W \otimes \mathrm{id}_C)(\phi(v) \otimes c) = T_W(\phi(v)) \otimes c = \phi(T_V(v)) \otimes c = \phi_K(T_V(v) \otimes c) = \phi_K((T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}_C)(v \otimes c)).
Since the simple tensors span V_C, this yields (T_W \otimes \mathrm{id}_C) \circ \phi_K = \phi_K \circ (T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}_C) as C-linear maps V_C \to W_C.

Step 4 (h_V is a positive definite Hermitian form). Define h_V: V_C \times V_C \to C by h_V(x, y) = h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K y), where \phi_K x denotes the image of x under the C-linear map \phi_K (this is the \phi x appearing in the statement, with \phi understood as its base change \phi_K).
- Sesquilinearity: h_W is sesquilinear (linear in the first variable, conjugate-linear in the second) and \phi_K is C-linear. For x, x', y, y' \in V_C and \alpha, \beta \in C:
  h_V(x+x', y) = h_W(\phi_K(x+x'), \phi_K y) = h_W(\phi_K x + \phi_K x', \phi_K y) = h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K y) + h_W(\phi_K x', \phi_K y) = h_V(x,y) + h_V(x',y);
  h_V(x, y+y') = h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K(y+y')) = h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K y + \phi_K y') = h_V(x,y) + h_V(x,y');
  h_V(\alpha x, y) = h_W(\phi_K(\alpha x), \phi_K y) = h_W(\alpha \phi_K x, \phi_K y) = \alpha\, h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K y) = \alpha\, h_V(x,y);
  h_V(x, \beta y) = h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K(\beta y)) = h_W(\phi_K x, \beta \phi_K y) = \overline{\beta}\, h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K y) = \overline{\beta}\, h_V(x,y).
  Hence h_V is sesquilinear.
- Hermitian symmetry: h_V(x, y) = h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K y) = \overline{h_W(\phi_K y, \phi_K x)} = \overline{h_V(y, x)}, using the Hermitian symmetry of h_W.
- Positive definiteness: For x \in V_C, h_V(x, x) = h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K x) \ge 0 because h_W is positive semidefinite. If h_V(x, x) = 0, then h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K x) = 0, so by positive definiteness of h_W we have \phi_K x = 0, and by injectivity of \phi_K (Step 2) we get x = 0. Thus h_V(x, x) > 0 for every x \ne 0.
Therefore h_V is a positive definite Hermitian form on V_C.

Step 5 (scaling identity). For all x, y \in V_C:
h_V((T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}_C) x, (T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}_C) y) = h_W(\phi_K((T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}_C) x), \phi_K((T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}_C) y))
= h_W((T_W \otimes \mathrm{id}_C)(\phi_K x), (T_W \otimes \mathrm{id}_C)(\phi_K y))   [by the intertwining relation of Step 3]
= q^m\, h_W(\phi_K x, \phi_K y)   [by the scaling hypothesis on h_W, applied to the pair (\phi_K x, \phi_K y) \in W_C \times W_C]
= q^m\, h_V(x, y).
This is the desired identity.

Combining Steps 4 and 5, h_V(x, y) = h_W(\phi x, \phi y) is a positive definite Hermitian form on V_C = V \otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell, \sigma} C satisfying h_V((T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}) x, (T_V \otimes \mathrm{id}) y) = q^m\, h_V(x, y) for all x, y \in V_C. This completes the proof.

statement: Let ell be a prime, let V and W be finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces, let T:V->V and S:W->W be Q_ell-linear automorphisms, and let phi:V->W be a Q_ell-linear injection such that S phi = phi T. If S is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), then T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof:
Let U = im(phi) = {phi(v) : v in V} subseteq W. We prove T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) in three steps.

Step 1 (U is S-stable and S|_U is an automorphism of U). First, U is a Q_ell-linear subspace of W: if u1 = phi(v1), u2 = phi(v2), and c in Q_ell, then u1 + c u2 = phi(v1) + phi(c v2) = phi(v1 + c v2) in U, since phi is Q_ell-linear. Next, S(U) subseteq U: for u = phi(v) in U, S(u) = S(phi(v)) = phi(T v) by the hypothesis S phi = phi T, and since T v in V, phi(T v) in U. Conversely, U subseteq S(U): let u = phi(v) in U. Since T is an automorphism of V, w := T^{-1}(v) in V exists, and then u = phi(v) = phi(T w) = S(phi w) by S phi = phi T, so u in S(U). Hence S(U) = U, and the restriction S|_U : U -> U is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of U. Also, the map phi : V -> U is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism: it is injective by hypothesis, and it is surjective onto U by the very definition of U as the image of phi, so it is bijective; a bijective Q_ell-linear map is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism with Q_ell-linear inverse phi^{-1} : U -> V. (We do not claim phi is an automorphism of V; that would require U = V.)

Edge case dim V = 0. If dim_{Q_ell} V = 0, then U = 0, and the restriction S|_U on the zero space is trivially diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) (the zero space has the empty basis, with respect to which the identity is diagonal). The argument below goes through uniformly in this case with n = 0, so no separate treatment is needed beyond noting this.

Step 2 (S|_U is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell)). Apply the proved lemma Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_440 with its V equal to our W, its T equal to our S, and its W equal to our U. The hypotheses are satisfied: W is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space, S in GL_{Q_ell}(W) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) by assumption, U is a Q_ell-linear subspace of W, and S(U) = U by Step 1. The lemma concludes that the restricted automorphism S|_U in GL_{Q_ell}(U) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).

Step 3 (transport the eigenbasis back to V via phi^{-1} tensor 1). Let n = dim_{Q_ell} V. Since phi : V -> U is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism (Step 1), dim_{Q_ell} U = n as well. Since S|_U is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) (Step 2), there exists a basis (e_1, ..., e_n) of U tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) of eigenvectors of S|_U tensor 1 : U tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) -> U tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell), i.e., (S|_U tensor 1)(e_i) = lambda_i e_i for i = 1, ..., n, with lambda_i in overline(Q_ell). (In the edge case n = 0 this is the empty basis of the zero space, and the following is vacuous but valid.)

Now define f_i = (phi^{-1} tensor 1)(e_i) in V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) for i = 1, ..., n. Because phi : V -> U is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism, phi tensor 1 : V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) -> U tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) is an overline(Q_ell)-linear isomorphism (tensoring an isomorphism with the identity is an isomorphism, with inverse phi^{-1} tensor 1). Hence (f_1, ..., f_n) = (phi^{-1} tensor 1)(e_1), ..., (phi^{-1} tensor 1)(e_n) is a basis of V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell}, since it is the image under the isomorphism phi^{-1} tensor 1 of the basis (e_1, ..., e_n) of U tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell).

We now compute the action of T tensor 1 on each f_i. First, as Q_ell-linear maps on V, we have the identity T = phi^{-1} o (S|_U) o phi: for v in V, (phi^{-1} o (S|_U) o phi)(v) = phi^{-1}(S(phi(v))) = phi^{-1}(phi(T v)) = T v, where the first equality uses S|_U = S on U and the second uses S phi = phi T. After base change to overline(Q_ell), this gives the identity of overline(Q_ell)-linear maps on V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell}
    T tensor 1 = (phi^{-1} tensor 1) o (S|_U tensor 1) o (phi tensor 1).
Applying this to f_i:
    (T tensor 1)(f_i) = (phi^{-1} tensor 1) o (S|_U tensor 1) o (phi tensor 1)(f_i).
By the definition f_i = (phi^{-1} tensor 1)(e_i), we have (phi tensor 1)(f_i) = (phi tensor 1) o (phi^{-1} tensor 1)(e_i) = e_i. Therefore
    (T tensor 1)(f_i) = (phi^{-1} tensor 1) o (S|_U tensor 1)(e_i) = (phi^{-1} tensor 1)(lambda_i e_i) = lambda_i (phi^{-1} tensor 1)(e_i) = lambda_i f_i,
using that S|_U tensor 1 is overline(Q_ell)-linear and (S|_U tensor 1)(e_i) = lambda_i e_i. Thus each f_i is an eigenvector of T tensor 1 with eigenvalue lambda_i, and (f_1, ..., f_n) is a basis of V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell} consisting of eigenvectors of T tensor 1.

Conclusion. The operator T tensor 1 : V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell} -> V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell} is diagonal with respect to the basis (f_1, ..., f_n) (its matrix in this basis is the diagonal matrix diag(lambda_1, ..., lambda_n)). This is precisely the statement that T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then beta(Fx,Fy)=q^{md} beta(x,y) for all x,y in H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
Setup. Let q=p^a be a prime power, ell != p a prime, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let F denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of X_k, and write F also for its induced automorphism of H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). We prove that the Poincare duality pairing beta on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) satisfies beta(Fx,Fy)=q^{md} beta(x,y) for all x,y in H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell).

Step 1 (the canonical trace isomorphism). The hypotheses of lemma_77 (id: eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77) are satisfied with Y=X: X is smooth, projective, geometrically connected, of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and ell != p. By part (a) of lemma_77, for the structure morphism f: X -> Spec F_{q^m}, the cycle-class/Gysin isomorphism Q_ell(d)[2d] -> Rf^! Q_ell induces a canonical isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces
  tr: H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d),
normalised by tr(cl(x)) = [k(x):F_{q^m}] for every closed point x of X, and tr is arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant, where F acts on Q_ell(-d) as multiplication by the positive rational number q^{md}. We use this canonical trace isomorphism as the definition of the Poincare duality trace; no separate Q_ell-valued trace, fundamental class, or dimension argument for H^{2d} is introduced or needed.

Step 2 (the similitude relation for the canonical pairing). Define the Q_ell(-d)-valued pairing
  <x,y> := tr(x cup y),  x,y in H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell).
Since 0 <= d <= 2d, part (b) of lemma_77 applies with n=d: the pairing <,>: H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d) is a PERFECT pairing of Q_ell-vector spaces (hence is the Poincare duality pairing), and it satisfies, for all x,y in H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell),
  <Fx,Fy> = q^{md} <x,y>,
where q^{md} acts on Q_ell(-d) by scalar multiplication. This is consistent with, and is the content of, the Frobenius-equivariance of tr in part (a), under which F on Q_ell(-d) is multiplication by q^{md}. No semisimplicity of F is used anywhere.

Step 3 (identification of the beta in the target statement). The target statement names beta the Poincare duality pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). There are two standard readings of this pairing, and we treat both.

Reading (i): beta is the canonical Q_ell(-d)-valued pairing, i.e. beta(x,y) = tr(x cup y) = <x,y>. Then the desired identity beta(Fx,Fy) = q^{md} beta(x,y) is exactly the equality of Step 2, an equality in Q_ell(-d) with q^{md} acting by scalar multiplication. Done.

Reading (ii): beta is the Q_ell-valued pairing obtained by composing the canonical pairing with a Q_ell-linear isomorphism phi: Q_ell(-d) -> Q_ell. Such an isomorphism exists because Q_ell(-d) is 1-dimensional over Q_ell; concretely, one fixes a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and thereby identifies the Tate twist Q_ell(-d) with Q_ell, exactly as is done in the standard normalisations. Then beta(x,y) := phi(<x,y>). Since q^{md} is an element of Q_ell and phi is Q_ell-linear, for every v in Q_ell(-d) one has phi(q^{md} v) = q^{md} phi(v). Applying phi to the equality of Step 2 gives, for all x,y,
  beta(Fx,Fy) = phi(<Fx,Fy>) = phi(q^{md} <x,y>) = q^{md} phi(<x,y>) = q^{md} beta(x,y).
Thus the identity holds in this reading as well, and it is independent of the choice of phi precisely because the scalar q^{md} lies in Q_ell.

Conclusion. In both readings of the Poincare duality pairing beta on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell), we have beta(Fx,Fy) = q^{md} beta(x,y) for all x,y in H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). This completes the proof. The only external input used is lemma_77, parts (a) and (b).

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Suppose that for every integer r with 0<=r<d, every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Then for every integer j>=1 with d-2j>=0, every eigenvalue of F on L^j P^{d-2j}, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}.
proof:
I have verified all three lemmas I need. Now I'll write the complete proof.

**Verification of the key relation:** Lemma `eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable` is stated for a variety over $\mathbb F_q$ with $q$-power Frobenius, giving $F\circ L=q\,L\circ F$. Since $q^m$ is itself a prime power ($p^{am}$), applying it with $q$ replaced by $q^m$ to my variety over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$ yields $F\circ L=q^mL\circ F$ for the $q^m$-power Frobenius $F$ — exactly what I need.

```json
{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/b69c89",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Miner/16d24b0281973336/305609", "eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable", "Miner/16d24b0281973336/c1a8d4"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "Fix an integer j>=1 with d-2j>=0, and set r=d-2j. Since j>=1 we have r=d-2j<=d-2<d, and since d-2j>=0 we have r>=0; hence 0<=r<d. We prove that every eigenvalue of F on L^j P^{d-2j} (viewed in overline(Q_ell)) has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}.

STEP 1 (Frobenius preserves P^r). By the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/305609, applied to our X, xi, L and the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F, we have F(P^r)=P^r.

STEP 2 (Frobenius intertwines with L up to the scalar q^m). The proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable is stated for a smooth projective variety over a prime-power field F_{q0} with q0-power Frobenius, and asserts F circ L = q0 L circ F on every cohomology group. The number q^m is itself a prime power (q^m=p^{am}); applying the lemma with q0=q^m to the variety X over F_{q^m}, its F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, its cycle class xi, and the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F, we obtain
    F circ L = q^m L circ F
on every H^i. We now iterate. Claim: for every s>=1, F circ L^s = q^{ms} L^s circ F. For s=1 this is the displayed relation. Assume it for s. Then
    F circ L^{s+1} = (F circ L^s) circ L = q^{ms}(L^s circ F) circ L = q^{ms} L^s circ (F circ L) = q^{ms} L^s circ (q^m L circ F) = q^{ms} q^m L^s circ L circ F = q^{m(s+1)} L^{s+1} circ F.
Taking s=j gives
    F circ L^j = q^{mj} L^j circ F.   (2)

STEP 3 (L^j is injective on H^r, and L^j:P^r -> L^j P^r is an isomorphism). By the hard Lefschetz hypothesis, with n=r the map L^{d-r}:H^r -> H^{2d-r} is an isomorphism. Since d-r = d-(d-2j) = 2j and 2d-r = 2d-(d-2j) = d+2j, this reads L^{2j}:H^r -> H^{d+2j} is an isomorphism, in particular injective. Now L^{2j}=L^j circ L^j. If L^j(x)=0 for some x in H^r, then L^{2j}(x)=L^j(L^j x)=L^j(0)=0, so x in ker(L^{2j})={0}; hence L^j is injective on H^r. By definition L^j P^r is the image of P^r under L^j, so the restriction phi := L^j|_{P^r}:P^r -> L^j P^r is surjective; and since L^j is injective on all of H^r, its restriction to P^r is injective. Hence phi:P^r -> L^j P^r is an isomorphism.

STEP 4 (F preserves L^j P^r and the induced operator is similar to q^{mj} F|_{P^r}). First, F maps L^j P^r into itself: for x in P^r, by (2) and Step 1, F(L^j x)=q^{mj} L^j(Fx) in L^j P^r, since Fx in P^r. (Frobenius is an automorphism of each H^i, being the pullback by the automorphism sigma:k->k, so this inclusion is in fact an equality F(L^j P^r)=L^j P^r, but only the inclusion is needed.) Now compute, for x in P^r, using (2) and Step 1:
    (F|_{L^j P^r} circ phi)(x) = F(L^j x) = q^{mj} L^j(Fx) = q^{mj} phi(Fx) = (q^{mj} phi circ F|_{P^r})(x).
Thus F|_{L^j P^r} circ phi = q^{mj} phi circ F|_{P^r}, i.e. F|_{L^j P^r} = phi circ (q^{mj} F|_{P^r}) circ phi^{-1}. Since phi is an isomorphism, F|_{L^j P^r} is similar to q^{mj} F|_{P^r}. Passing to scalars over overline(Q_ell) (similarity is preserved under any field extension, and the minimal polynomial is unchanged), the multiset of eigenvalues of F|_{L^j P^r} viewed in overline(Q_ell) is exactly { q^{mj} lambda : lambda runs over the eigenvalues of F|_{P^r} viewed in overline(Q_ell) }.

STEP 5 (Weil absolute values). The hypothesis states that every eigenvalue of F on H^r (with r<d) viewed in overline(Q_ell) has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Combined with Step 1 (F(P^r)=P^r), the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/c1a8d4 applies to our X, xi, L, F and r, and yields: every eigenvalue of F|_{P^r}, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.

Now let mu be any eigenvalue of F|_{L^j P^r} viewed in overline(Q_ell). By Step 4, mu=q^{mj} lambda for some eigenvalue lambda of F|_{P^r} viewed in overline(Q_ell). The Weil absolute value |.|_W on overline(Q_ell) is multiplicative, and for the positive rational q^{mj} we have |q^{mj}|_W=q^{mj}. Hence
    |mu|_W = |q^{mj} lambda|_W = |q^{mj}|_W |lambda|_W = q^{mj} * q^{mr/2} = q^{mj+mr/2}.
Finally, mj+mr/2 = m(j+r/2) = m(j+(d-2j)/2) = m(j+d/2-j) = md/2. Therefore |mu|_W = q^{md/2}.

Since mu was an arbitrary eigenvalue of F on L^j P^{d-2j}, every such eigenvalue has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}. As j was an arbitrary integer >=1 with d-2j>=0, the claim holds for all such j. This completes the proof."
}
```
