statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, X a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), let tr_X be the Poincare duality trace, and put beta_r(x,y)=tr_X(x cup L^{d-r}y) for x,y in H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then for every x in P^r and every integer n>=1, beta_r(x,F^n x)+(-1)^r q^{mrn} beta_r(x,F^{-n}x)=2 beta_r(x,F^n x).
proof: Let D be the F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor whose untwisted cycle class is xi. We write F also for the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on all cohomology groups; its restriction to H^r is the operator named F in the statement. First we justify the scaling of xi. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_291 with the base prime power q0 := q^m, with the same variety X over F_{q0}, with j := 1, with m0 := 1, and with z := D, which is a codimension-1 cycle on X_{F_{q0}}. In that lemma the q0-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) is exactly our F, and cl(D) is the image of the Q_ell(1)-cycle class under the fixed identification Q_ell(1) ~ Q_ell that defines xi in the target. Hence F(xi) = q0 xi = q^m xi. No descent to F_q is used. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, applied with base field F_{q^m} and sigma(c)=c^{q^m}, F is an invertible Q_ell-linear automorphism on every H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell), and F^(-1) is the geometric Frobenius. Functoriality of the cup product for the pullback morphism defining F makes F a ring automorphism of the cohomology ring, with F(1)=1 and F(a cup b)=F(a) cup F(b). For any s>=0 and any y in H^t_et(X_k,Q_ell), L^s y = xi^s cup y, so F(L^s y) = F(xi^s cup y) = F(xi)^s cup F(y) = (q^m xi)^s cup F(y) = q^{ms} L^s F(y). In particular, if M := L^{d-r+1}, then F(M y) = q^{m(d-r+1)} M(F y) for all y in H^r. We now show F and F^(-1) preserve P^r = ker(M). If y in P^r, then M y=0, so 0=F(M y)=q^{m(d-r+1)}M(F y), hence F y in P^r. For F^(-1), put z=F^(-1)(y) in the displayed identity: F(M z)=q^{m(d-r+1)}M(y). If y in P^r, then M(y)=0, so F(M z)=0; since F is injective on H^{2d-r+2}, M z=0, i.e. F^(-1)(y) in P^r. Thus F^n(x) and F^(-n)(x) lie in P^r for every n>=1. Next compute the similitude factor of beta_r under F. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, the Poincare trace is Frobenius equivariant: in the untwisted coordinates of the target, tr_X(Fw)=q^{md} tr_X(w) for w in H^{2d}. Therefore for u,v in H^r, beta_r(Fu,Fv)=tr_X(Fu cup L^{d-r} Fv). Using F(L^{d-r}v)=q^{m(d-r)} L^{d-r}Fv, and since ell != p makes q^{m(d-r)} invertible in Q_ell, we get L^{d-r}Fv = q^(-m(d-r)) F(L^{d-r}v). Hence, by Q_ell-linearity of tr_X, beta_r(Fu,Fv)=q^(-m(d-r)) tr_X(F(u cup L^{d-r}v)) = q^(-m(d-r)) q^{md} tr_X(u cup L^{d-r}v) = q^{mr} beta_r(u,v). Iterating by induction on n gives beta_r(F^n u,F^n v)=q^{mrn} beta_r(u,v). Finally, by Miner/16d24b0281973336/2e4606, for all a,b in P^r one has beta_r(a,b)=(-1)^r beta_r(b,a). Apply this to a=x and b=F^(-n)(x), both in P^r: beta_r(x,F^(-n)(x))=(-1)^r beta_r(F^(-n)(x),x). Apply the iterated similitude with u=F^(-n)(x) and v=x: beta_r(x,F^n x)=beta_r(F^n(F^(-n)(x)),F^n x)=q^{mrn} beta_r(F^(-n)(x),x). Therefore beta_r(F^(-n)(x),x)=q^(-mrn) beta_r(x,F^n x), and hence beta_r(x,F^(-n)(x))=(-1)^r q^(-mrn) beta_r(x,F^n x). Substituting into the left side yields beta_r(x,F^n x)+(-1)^r q^{mrn} [(-1)^r q^(-mrn) beta_r(x,F^n x)] = beta_r(x,F^n x)+beta_r(x,F^n x)=2 beta_r(x,F^n x). This proves the claim.

statement: Let ell be a prime, let V and W be finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces, let A:V->W be Q_ell-linear, let T_V:V->V and T_W:W->W be Q_ell-linear automorphisms, and let c in Q_ell^* such that T_W A = c A T_V. If T_V is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), then T_W is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on im(A).
proof:
We prove that the restriction T_W|_{im(A)} is diagonalizable over K = overline(Q_ell). All vector spaces are finite-dimensional over Q_ell.

Step 1 (T_W preserves im(A)). For any v in V, T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V v) by the hypothesis T_W A = c A T_V. Since T_V v in V, A(T_V v) in im(A), so T_W(A(v)) in im(A). Hence T_W(im(A)) subseteq im(A), and T_W|_{im(A)}: im(A) -> im(A) is a well-defined Q_ell-linear endomorphism. (In fact it is an automorphism of im(A) since T_W is invertible and preserves im(A), but we only need it to be an endomorphism.) The edge case im(A) = {0} is trivial: the zero endomorphism on the zero space is diagonalizable, so assume im(A) != {0} below if desired; the argument works uniformly.

Step 2 (reduce to base change over K). Let V_K = V tensor_{Q_ell} K and W_K = W tensor_{Q_ell} K, and write A_K, T_{V,K}, T_{W,K} for the base-changed maps. The relation T_W A = c A T_V is Q_ell-linear and involves only scalar multiplication by c, so after tensoring with K we get T_{W,K} A_K = c A_K T_{V,K}. The assumption that T_V is diagonalizable over K means exactly that T_{V,K} is diagonalizable over K. Also, T_W|_{im(A)} is diagonalizable over K if and only if (T_W|_{im(A)}) tensor id_K is diagonalizable over K; and (T_W|_{im(A)}) tensor id_K = T_{W,K}|_{im(A) tensor K}. Finally, since K/Q_ell is a field extension (hence flat), base change preserves images: im(A_K) = im(A) tensor_{Q_ell} K. Indeed, factoring A = j o p with p: V -> im(A) surjective and j: im(A) -> W the inclusion, flatness gives that p_K: V_K -> im(A)_K is surjective, so im(A_K) = image(p_K o j_K) = im(A)_K = im(A) tensor K. Therefore it suffices to prove that T_{W,K} is diagonalizable over K on the subspace im(A_K) of W_K.

Step 3 (decompose V_K into eigenspaces of T_{V,K}). Since T_{V,K} is diagonalizable over K, its spectrum sigma = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_r} is a finite subset of K and V_K = direct sum_{i=1}^r E_{lambda_i} where E_{lambda_i} = ker(T_{V,K} - lambda_i id_{V_K}), a direct sum (eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues of a diagonalizable operator are in direct sum and span the space).

Step 4 (images of eigenspaces land in eigenspaces of T_{W,K}). Fix i and let w = A_K(v) with v in E_{lambda_i}. Then T_{W,K}(w) = T_{W,K} A_K(v) = c A_K T_{V,K}(v) = c A_K(lambda_i v) = c lambda_i A_K(v) = c lambda_i w. Thus A_K(E_{lambda_i}) subseteq ker(T_{W,K} - c lambda_i id_{W_K}) =: F_{c lambda_i}. In particular A_K(E_{lambda_i}) is contained in the eigenspace of T_{W,K} for the eigenvalue c lambda_i.

Step 5 (im(A_K) lies in a direct sum of eigenspaces of T_{W,K}). Since V_K = sum_i E_{lambda_i}, im(A_K) = A_K(V_K) = sum_i A_K(E_{lambda_i) subseteq sum_i F_{c lambda_i}. Because c in Q_ell^* is nonzero, the numbers c lambda_i for i = 1,...,r are pairwise distinct (lambda_i != lambda_j implies c lambda_i != c lambda_j). The eigenspaces F_{c lambda_i} of T_{W,K} for the distinct eigenvalues c lambda_1,...,c lambda_r are in direct sum: if w = sum_i w_i with w_i in F_{c lambda_i} and w = 0, then applying the operator prod_{j != i} (T_{W,K} - c lambda_j id) to w gives 0 = prod_{j != i}(c lambda_i - c lambda_j) w_i, and the scalar prod_{j != i}(c lambda_i - c lambda_j) is nonzero, so w_i = 0. Hence M := sum_i F_{c lambda_i} is a direct sum, and T_{W,K}|_M is diagonalizable (M is a direct sum of eigenspaces of T_{W,K}). We have im(A_K) subseteq M.

Step 6 (a T_{W,K}-stable subspace of a diagonalizable direct sum of eigenspaces is diagonalizable). We use that im(A_K) is T_{W,K}-stable: this is the base change of Step 1, i.e. T_{W,K}(im(A_K)) = T_{W,K}(im(A) tensor K) = (T_W(im(A))) tensor K subseteq im(A) tensor K = im(A_K). Now let U = im(A_K) subseteq M. For each i, the spectral projection P_i: M -> F_{c lambda_i} (projection onto the c lambda_i-eigenspace along the other summands) is a polynomial in T_{W,K}|_M: explicitly P_i = prod_{j != i} (T_{W,K}|_M - c lambda_j id)/(c lambda_i - c lambda_j), a polynomial in T_{W,K}|_M with coefficients in K (the scalars c lambda_j lie in K). Since U is stable under T_{W,K}|_M, U is stable under every polynomial in T_{W,K}|_M, in particular under P_i. Therefore for any u in U, u = sum_i P_i(u) with P_i(u) in U cap F_{c lambda_i}. Hence U = sum_i (U cap F_{c lambda_i}). Because the F_{c lambda_i} are in direct sum, the subspaces U cap F_{c lambda_i} are also in direct sum, so U = direct sum_i (U cap F_{c lambda_i}). On each U cap F_{c lambda_i}, T_{W,K} acts by the scalar c lambda_i, so each U cap F_{c lambda_i} is an eigenspace of T_{W,K}|_U. Thus U = im(A_K) is a direct sum of eigenspaces of T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)}, which means T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)} is diagonalizable over K.

Step 7 (conclusion). From Step 6, T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)} is diagonalizable over K. By the equivalences in Step 2, this is exactly the statement that T_W|_{im(A)} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). This completes the proof.

Remark on the edge cases: if im(A) = {0}, then im(A_K) = {0} and T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)} is the zero map on the zero space, trivially diagonalizable, so the conclusion holds. If A = 0 this is the same case. No further degeneracy occurs because c != 0 guarantees the eigenvalues c lambda_i remain distinct, keeping the eigenspace decomposition in Step 5 a genuine direct sum.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Suppose F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for 0<=r<d. Then for every integer j>=1 with d-2j>=0, F on L^j P^{d-2j} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Let Q = q^m. Fix an integer j >= 1 with r = d - 2j >= 0. We prove that F on L^j P^r is diagonalizable over Qbar_l. By the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/305609, the subspace P^r is stable under F, i.e. F(P^r) = P^r. Now apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable to the prime power Q and to the variety X over F_Q, with the given very ample divisor and its cycle class xi. The Frobenius appearing in that lemma is the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius, which is exactly the operator F in the statement. It gives F L = Q L F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_l). By induction from this relation we obtain F L^j = Q^j L^j F on H^r. The hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n = r gives that L^{2j}: H^r_et(X_k,Q_l) -> H^{d+2j}_et(X_k,Q_l) is an isomorphism, hence injective. If x in P^r satisfies L^j x = 0, then L^{2j} x = L^j(L^j x) = 0, so x = 0. Thus phi = L^j restricted to P^r is an isomorphism from P^r onto L^j P^r. By hypothesis F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_l) is diagonalizable over Qbar_l. Since P^r is F-stable, F|_{P^r} is diagonalizable over Qbar_l: after scalar extension to Qbar_l, write V = H^r_et(X_k,Q_l) tensor Qbar_l and W = P^r tensor Qbar_l; the operator T = F tensor id on V is diagonalizable, so V is the direct sum of its eigenspaces V_lambda; the eigenspace projections are polynomial functions in T and hence preserve the T-stable subspace W, so W is the direct sum of W intersect V_lambda and is spanned by eigenvectors. For y in L^j P^r write y = phi(x) = L^j x with x in P^r. Then F(y) = F(L^j x) = Q^j L^j F(x) = phi(Q^j F(x)), because F(x) lies in P^r. Hence F|_{L^j P^r} = phi (Q^j F|_{P^r}) phi^{-1}. The scalar Q^j is nonzero in Q_l because ell != p, and a nonzero scalar multiple of a diagonalizable operator is diagonalizable over Qbar_l (the same eigenvectors work). Conjugation by an isomorphism preserves diagonalizability. Therefore F|_{L^j P^r} is diagonalizable over Qbar_l. Since j was arbitrary with d - 2j >= 0, the claim follows.

statement: Let ell be a prime, let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C be an embedding, let r>0 be a real number, let V and W be finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces, let A:V->W be Q_ell-linear, let T_V:V->V and T_W:W->W be Q_ell-linear automorphisms, and let c in Q_ell^* such that T_W A = c A T_V. If every eigenvalue alpha of T_V satisfies |sigma(alpha)|=r, then every eigenvalue beta of T_W on im(A) satisfies |sigma(beta)|=|sigma(c)| r.
proof:
We prove the statement by pure linear algebra over Q_ell, reducing the scalar-twisted intertwining relation to an ordinary conjugacy on a quotient space, then using the standard fact that the spectrum of an induced quotient operator is contained in the spectrum of the original operator.

SETUP AND NOTATION. Let K = ker(A) \subseteq V. Write S := T_W|_{im(A)} for the restriction of T_W to im(A) (its well-definedness as a map im(A)->im(A) is established in Step 1). All operators below are Q_ell-linear. Eigenvalues are taken in the algebraic closure overline(Q_ell); the given embedding sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C is a field embedding, hence a ring homomorphism, so sigma(xy)=sigma(x)sigma(y) and sigma(x+y)=sigma(x)+sigma(y) for all x,y in overline(Q_ell).

STEP 0 (edge case). If im(A) = {0}, then S is the zero map on the zero vector space, whose characteristic polynomial is 1 (degree 0) and which therefore has no eigenvalues in overline(Q_ell). The assertion 'every eigenvalue beta of T_W on im(A) satisfies |sigma(beta)|=|sigma(c)| r' is then vacuously true. Henceforth assume im(A) != {0}.

STEP 1 (T_W preserves im(A)). Let y in im(A); then y = A(v) for some v in V. By the hypothesis T_W A = c A T_V we have T_W(y) = T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V(v)). Since T_V(v) in V, the element A(T_V(v)) lies in im(A); as im(A) is a Q_ell-subspace of W and c in Q_ell^*, the scalar multiple c A(T_V(v)) also lies in im(A). Thus T_W(im(A)) \subseteq im(A), so the restriction S := T_W|_{im(A)}:im(A)->im(A) is well-defined. Because T_W is an automorphism of W and im(A) is T_W-stable, S is an automorphism of im(A) (its inverse is (T_W^{-1})|_{im(A)}).

STEP 2 (T_V preserves K = ker(A)). Let v in K, so A(v)=0. Applying the intertwining relation to v gives T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V(v)), i.e. T_W(0) = c A(T_V(v)), so c A(T_V(v)) = 0. Since c != 0, A(T_V(v)) = 0, hence T_V(v) in K. Thus T_V(K) \subseteq K, i.e. K is T_V-stable.

STEP 3 (quotient isomorphism). The map A:V->im(A) is surjective by definition of the image, and its kernel is K. By the first isomorphism theorem it induces a Q_ell-linear isomorphism \\bar{A}:V/K -> im(A) given by \\bar{A}(v+K) = A(v). This is well-defined and bijective: well-definedness follows because if v+K = v'+K then v-v' in K so A(v)-A(v')=0; surjectivity is the definition of im(A); injectivity follows because ker(\\bar{A}) = {v+K : A(v)=0} = K/(K) = {0}.

STEP 4 (induced operator on V/K). Since K is T_V-stable (Step 2), T_V induces a Q_ell-linear operator \\bar{T}_V:V/K -> V/K given by \\bar{T}_V(v+K) = T_V(v)+K. This is well-defined: if v+K = v'+K then v-v' in K and T_V(v)-T_V(v') in T_V(K) \subseteq K, so T_V(v)+K = T_V(v')+K. It is an automorphism because T_V is.

STEP 5 (conjugacy). We claim S \\circ \\bar{A} = c \\bar{A} \\circ \\bar{T}_V. For any v+K in V/K: \\bar{A}(\\bar{T}_V(v+K)) = \\bar{A}(T_V(v)+K) = A(T_V(v)). On the other hand S(\\bar{A}(v+K)) = S(A(v)) = T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V(v)) by the intertwining relation. Hence S\\circ\\bar{A}(v+K) = c A(T_V(v)) = c \\bar{A}(\\bar{T}_V(v+K)), and the claim follows. Since \\bar{A} is an isomorphism, this is equivalent to S = c \\bar{A} \\circ \\bar{T}_V \\circ \\bar{A}^{-1}. Thus S is similar (conjugate) to the operator c\\bar{T}_V on V/K.

STEP 6 (spectrum of S). Similar operators over Q_ell have identical characteristic polynomials, hence identical multisets of eigenvalues in overline(Q_ell) (with multiplicity). Therefore the multiset of eigenvalues of S equals the multiset of eigenvalues of c\\bar{T}_V. For any Q_ell-linear operator N on a finite-dimensional space and any nonzero scalar c in Q_ell, the eigenvalues of cN are exactly {c\\cdot\\lambda : \\lambda an eigenvalue of N}: indeed if Nx = \\lambda x with x != 0 then (cN)x = (c\\lambda)x, and conversely if (cN)x = \\mu x with x != 0 then N x = (\\mu/c) x since c != 0. Equivalently, with \\lambda_1,...,\\lambda_s the eigenvalues of \\bar{T}_V, the characteristic polynomial of c\\bar{T}_V is \\prod_i (t - c\\lambda_i). Consequently every eigenvalue beta of S (equivalently of T_W on im(A)) is of the form beta = c\\cdot\\mu for some eigenvalue \\mu of \\bar{T}_V in overline(Q_ell).

STEP 7 (spectrum of \\bar{T}_V is contained in spectrum of T_V). We prove the general fact that the eigenvalues of the induced operator on the quotient are a subset of the eigenvalues of the original operator, by an explicit block-matrix computation. Let n = dim V and k = dim K. Choose a Q_ell-basis (e_1,...,e_n) of V such that (e_1,...,e_k) is a basis of K. Because K is T_V-stable (Step 2), T_V(e_i) in K for i = 1,...,k, so in this basis the matrix of T_V has block upper-triangular form [T_V] = [[B, C],[0, D]], where B is k x k, C is k x (n-k), 0 is (n-k) x k, and D is (n-k) x (n-k). The block B represents T_V|_K, and the block D represents the induced operator \\bar{T}_V on V/K with respect to the induced basis (e_{k+1}+K,...,e_n+K): indeed for j > k, \\bar{T}_V(e_j+K) = T_V(e_j)+K, and the V/K-component of T_V(e_j) is read off from the last n-k coordinates, which are D times the coordinate vector. Hence \\chi_{\\bar{T}_V}(t) = det(t I_{n-k} - D). The characteristic polynomial of T_V is \\chi_{T_V}(t) = det(t I_n - [T_V]) = det([[tI_k - B, -C],[0, tI_{n-k} - D]]) = det(tI_k - B)\\cdot det(tI_{n-k} - D) = \\chi_{T_V|_K}(t)\\cdot\\chi_{\\bar{T}_V}(t), using that the determinant of a block upper-triangular matrix is the product of the determinants of the diagonal blocks. Thus \\chi_{\\bar{T}_V} divides \\chi_{T_V} in Q_ell[t]. Any eigenvalue \\mu of \\bar{T}_V is a root of \\chi_{\\bar{T}_V} in overline(Q_ell), hence a root of \\chi_{T_V} in overline(Q_ell), hence an eigenvalue of T_V. So Spec(\\bar{T}_V) \\subseteq Spec(T_V).

STEP 8 (conclusion). Let beta be any eigenvalue of T_W on im(A) = im(A), i.e. any eigenvalue of S in overline(Q_ell). By Step 6, beta = c\\cdot\\mu for some eigenvalue \\mu of \\bar{T}_V. By Step 7, \\mu is an eigenvalue of T_V, so by the hypothesis |sigma(\\mu)| = r. Since sigma is a ring homomorphism, sigma(beta) = sigma(c\\cdot\\mu) = sigma(c)\\cdot sigma(\\mu). Taking complex absolute values, |sigma(beta)| = |sigma(c)\\cdot sigma(\\mu)| = |sigma(c)|\\cdot|sigma(\\mu)| = |sigma(c)|\\cdot r. This holds for every eigenvalue beta of T_W on im(A), completing the proof. (The edge case im(A)={0} was handled in Step 0.)

REMARK ON THE ROLE OF THE HYPOTHESES. The assumption that T_V and T_W are automorphisms guarantees S is an automorphism of im(A) (Step 1) and that \\bar{T}_V is an automorphism (Step 4), though only the Q_ell-linearity and the intertwining relation T_W A = c A T_V with c != 0 are used to obtain the conjugacy (Step 5) and the spectral inclusion (Steps 6-7). The condition c in Q_ell^* (nonzero) is used in Steps 2, 6 to divide by c. The number r > 0 and the embedding sigma enter only in the final absolute-value computation of Step 8, where multiplicativity of sigma and of the complex absolute value are the only properties used.
